entities.summary:
The black hole is an astronomical object so massive that anything falling into it, including light, cannot escape its gravity. This phenomenon was first described by John Michell in 1783, who hypothesized that a star could collapse into a region of space where the gravitational pull is so strong that not even light can escape.

The concept of black holes has since been extensively studied and developed by scientists such as David Finkelstein, Martin Schwarzschild, and Roger Penrose. Their work built upon Michell's ideas and led to a deeper understanding of these mysterious objects in the universe.

The first direct observation of a black hole was made in 2019 by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) project, which captured an image of the supermassive black hole at the center of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87).
